agent_explanations_oldest_first.text:
On `hold_1`, E4 is harmful but much less so than on DEV: 20.31% against 17.97%, a paired change of -2.34 ± 2.07, with 11 answers going wrong to right and 17 right to wrong. That's about 1.1 standard errors, against -6.25 on DEV.

Before running the second HOLDOUT set, I'll check whether E4 still flips Let openings to Here as it did on DEV. If many fewer problems flipped, the smaller loss is just less exposure. If a similar number flipped but those flipped answers lost less than on DEV (24.3% to 10.7% there), the per-problem harm of the Here register was overestimated on DEV. I'll split the answers by opener in each model and compare accuracy within each group.

On HOLDOUT, the register's causal effect replicates where it should. E4 turned 109 of the 137 Let openings into Here:

| Group | n | Original | E4 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flipped from Let to Here | 109 | 20.2% | 11.9% | -8.26 ± 4.15 |
| Kept Let | 28 | 35.7% | 35.7% | 0 |
| Opens with Here naturally | 119 | 16.8% | 19.3% | +2.52 ± 1.87 |

The flipped group's loss matches DEV, where it fell from 24.3% to 10.7%.

The natural-Here group gained a little, though no opener changed there. On DEV, the unflipped problems moved -1.3 instead, so I read that gain as noise, and it offsets part of the loss in the overall -2.3.

So the account holds on held-out problems. Forcing a Let-natural problem into the Here register costs about 8-14 points, while the opposite flip doesn't help, as E1 showed on DEV and E5 on HOLDOUT (-0.56 ± 2.30 on 354 flipped problems). The model's own choice of register is about as good as any I can impose.

I'll run E4 once more, on `hold_2`, to bring the flipped group to about 220 problems and its standard error to about 3. That would make this the one mechanistic effect in the study confirmed at about 3 standard errors on held-out data. It's a confirmation only: nothing is being chosen on HOLDOUT, and the original stays the submission.

E4 is still the only active edit, and the notes record the plan. This generation pass runs E4 against the original on `hold_2` (256 HOLDOUT problems), as a held-out confirmation only. I'll pool the flipped group with `hold_1`. The prediction is again a clear loss among problems pushed from Let to Here, bringing the pooled flipped effect to about -8 points at about 3 standard errors.

If the flipped group shows no loss on this set, the register effect is weaker than DEV suggested, and I'll report it at the pooled size rather than as confirmed.

On `hold_2`, E4 again costs a little overall: 20.70% against 19.53%, -1.17 ± 1.88, with 10 answers going wrong to right and 13 right to wrong. The overall number mixes the problems that flipped register with those that didn't, so the opener split decides whether the effect replicates.

I'll split this pass by opener, as before, and then pool the flipped groups of both HOLDOUT passes with paired standard errors. Confirmation needs the pooled flipped group to lose clearly, at about -8 points and roughly 3 standard errors from zero. If the loss on `hold_2` is small, I'll report the pooled size as it stands and soften the claim.
